item.title: Couple bought a broken Eichler home; now it’s worth $2.75 million
item.description: A magnificent example of midcentury modern architecture, this rare 1971 Eichler home in San Anselmo is listed at $2.75 million. Boasting four bedrooms, it has been tastefully renovated since its acquisition in 2015, showcasing an inviting indoor-outdoor aesthetic, a contemporary kitchen, and a sparkling pool. This home blends vibrant living spaces, making it perfect for families and older adults seeking style and comfort. Fuente: The Times of India - World.

item.title: More than 1,000 children dead in Bangladesh measles crisis
item.description: The death toll from measles in Bangladesh topped 1,000 children since March, health officials said on Wednesday, admitting that failures in a vaccination drive could have fuelled the outbreak. The South Asian nation of 170 million has recorded 1,002 deaths and 187,484 infections among children, making this year’s outbreak the country’s deadliest in decades, according to the Directorate General of Health Services (DGHS). Measles is highly contagious, spreading through coughs and sneezes, and has... Fuente: South China Morning Post.

The Pardons Board, chaired by the country’s king, is expected to meet on Friday to discuss potentially granting Najib clemency from his ongoing jail sentence for corruption linked to the multibillion-dollar 1MDB scandal,... item.title: Indonesia has new food safety rules for free meals. Why are students still falling ill?
item.description: Indonesian President Prabowo Subianto’s flagship free nutritious meals programme is facing renewed scrutiny after yet another wave of mass food poisoning that affected more than 2,000 students, raising questions about why safeguards on paper fail to translate to food safety on the ground. A series of illnesses were reported in Java, Sumatra, and Sulawesi in the past week. The latest was on Tuesday in Rembang, Central Java, where 200 students of an Islamic school showed symptoms of food poisoning... Fuente: South China Morning Post.

item.title: In 1973, Montana released a gall fly to control spotted knapweed; decades later...
item.description: Controlling invasive spotted knapweed biologically has initiated an unexpected ecological chain reaction. Gall flies, introduced as a control measure, have turned into a vital winter food source for deer mice, causing a surge in their populations and an uptick in hantavirus spread. Areas dense with knapweed report more infected mice than those with native grasslands. Fuente: The Times of India - World.

item.title: Hidden gut bacteria populations linked to ageing, cancer and type 2 diabetes may spread worldwide
item.description: Scientists led by the University of Vienna have found hidden populations within common gut bacteria, some of which are linked to ageing, colorectal cancer, inflammatory bowel disease and type 2 diabetes. The study also found evidence that certain bacterial populations can spread between people and across continents within a few decades, suggesting the gut microbiome may be more transmissible and dynamic than previously thought. Fuente: The Times of India - World.

item.title: Hong Kong seizes HK$1.4b suspected drugs over summer as traffickers target students
item.description: Hong Kong customs has smashed an international drug trafficking network over the summer, seizing 6.1 tonnes of suspected narcotics worth more than HK$1.4 billion (US$178.5 million) and arresting 150 people as syndicates actively recruited students during the holiday period.
